PRICES. Every price in this report is Friday 2026-10-09's close, taken pre-open on Monday 2026-10-12 and re-quoted at synthesis — a closed market, not stale data. Levels are all set off that close. WHAT COULD NOT BE FETCHED, and it is a lot this run. (1) No index or futures context at all: Yahoo's chart API returned HTTP 429 for ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, ES, NQ, DXY, gold and WTI, and finnhub refuses index CFDs, so SPY and QQQ closes stand in for the tape and the VIX and DXY levels are null rather than guessed. (2) No options-implied-move check on any finalist — the yahoo-options endpoint returned 401 — so not one idea here has been tested against what the straddle prices, which matters most for UNH and GE, both of which are underwritten around a print. (3) No short-interest or days-to-cover read on anything (api.nasdaq.com read timeout). (4) Brent-WTI is not stated: sources ranged from $7 to $29 and one printed an obvious outlier, so the spread is recorded as wide and volatile, which is all the sources support. Brent ~$105 and WTI ~$92 are news-reported figures, labelled as such in market_context.levels rather than presented as fetched quotes.

EVENT CONTRACTS: no idea, and the reason is no edge rather than no data. market_data.py events is broken, not down — it reads Kalshi's retired yes_bid/yes_ask/last_price/volume/open_interest fields instead of the current *_dollars and *_fp names, and it never paginates or filters server-side, so it only ever sees an arbitrary first 200 open markets. Research worked around it by querying Kalshi directly with event_ticker=, which returned the full 21-strike CPI ladder and the Fed path on the first attempt: P(<=3.5) 12%, P(3.6) 36%, P(3.7) 40.5%, P(>=3.8) 11.5%, modal 3.7%. That is the market pricing the same street consensus (3.7%) and Cleveland Fed nowcast (~3.6%) that research was reading, so there is no probability disagreement to publish, and October crude is irrelevant to a September print. Fixing that function is the highest-value code change available to this pipeline — it is why the event lane keeps coming up empty.

CONCENTRATION, which is this report's main weakness. Three of the six ideas — ITA, HII, GE — are aerospace and defense, exactly the correlation cap of 3, and ITA holds both GE and HII, so the basket overlaps the two single names. Their drivers do differ (a sector risk-premium swing, a naval shipbuilding monopoly re-rating, a commercial-aero aftermarket print) but they will sell off together, and a reader sizing all three is making one bet three times. The skew is not manufactured: on Friday's close the only names screening with improving analyst revisions were in aerospace, defense and steel (HII +5.9pp, RTX +3.4pp, STLD +1.7pp, CLF +21.3pp) while everything else screened deteriorated (LRN -11.1, TRV -7.6, IBKR -7.2, CMC -3.9, AA -1.2) and GE was exactly flat. market_context.summary: Monday 2026-10-12, pre-open. Columbus Day: US equities trade, the cash Treasury market is closed, so rate-sensitive moves today are futures- and ETF-driven only. The dominant driver is Middle East oil supply risk, now two months old and escalating rather than a one-day headline: Houthi strikes hit Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport again on Sunday after a Saturday strike that killed 12 and injured 300+, the airport is shut, Saudi Arabia flew 120+ sorties in 24 hours and said oil supply continues to flow, Trump said the US is weighing joining operations against the Houthis, and a tanker was attacked near Hormuz. Brent is around $105 and WTI around $92 on news reports. Iran called Washington's reply to its seven-condition Hormuz proposal insufficient, so the 22 September 'Hormuz reopening' trade that de-rated defense has been falsified. Rates are the other half of the regime: the 10y is 5.22% against a 3.88% policy rate, a steep term-premium curve, with headline CPI due Wednesday at a consensus 3.7% and Kalshi pricing an October hold at 84% and a December 25bp hike at 71-74%. That combination is why gold is -12.6% off its high in the middle of a regional war, and why builders, REITs and long duration are all leaning into a headwind. Friday closed risk-on at the index level (SPY +0.60%, QQQ +0.49%) but the single clearest dislocation on the board is backwards from the news: defense primes are de-rating through an escalating war, NOC -26.4% off its high, RTX -18%, GD -17%, LMT -16.8%, all below both their 20- and 50-day averages.

recommendations.thesis: Huntington Ingalls is the only builder of US nuclear submarines and aircraft carriers, it has a record $57.3bn backlog worth 4.2 years of revenue, and in its Q2 FY2026 release it beat by 37%, lifted segment margin to 6.6% from 5.6%, raised FY26 shipbuilding revenue guidance to $10.2-10.4bn and raised the low end of its margin guidance — and the stock is down 32% from its high, 3% above a 120-day low, at ~14.6x annualised H1 EPS against GD at 19.5x, LMT 16.9x and NOC 16.6x. The de-rating that hit the primes is a bet on US defense budget growth slowing after FY2027; applying it to the one franchise with a 20-year, single-source order book and no competitor is the mispricing.
recommendations.key_risk: Free cash flow was negative $150M in Q2 against positive $730M a year earlier. HII is a capital-intensive shipbuilder ramping two submarine classes at once, and if the working-capital drain is structural rather than timing, the reaffirmed $500-600M FY26 free cash flow is missed and a 14.6x multiple is not cheap for a business that cannot fund its own ramp. The second risk is execution: Q1 margin fell to 5.6% on pre-COVID-era fixed-price contracts, and that is the same class of problem now costing Northrop ~$2.0bn on B-21. Invalidation, stated as a condition rather than a price: FY26 free cash flow coming in below the reaffirmed $500-600M guide, or shipbuilding segment margin printing below the 6.0% low end of guidance for two consecutive quarters. Either means the $57.3bn backlog is not converting at the margin the thesis is underwritten on, and the thesis is wrong regardless of where the share price sits. Third, added by the red team: HII does not report inside 30 sessions on the fetched calendar, while NOC and RTX print 2026-10-20 and LMT and GD 2026-10-22. A sector-wide guide-down on post-FY2027 budget growth in that week would mark HII down with the primes weeks before it gets to answer with its own backlog conversion, and the accumulation plan has to be able to sit through that rather than be stopped out of it — which is the reason this row carries a bear case and no stop.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a shipbuilding monopoly is a monopsony customer in disguise: HII has exactly one buyer, the Navy sets the price, and margin has sat at 5-7% for years against 10%+ at the primes, so a persistent discount to GD and LMT is the correct price for a business with no pricing power rather than an error. The answer is that the discount is not being argued away, it is being sized — the target is 16.5x, still below GD today, on earnings carried by a backlog that is already contracted rather than forecast. The thesis does not need HII to earn prime-like margins; it needs 6.5-8% on roughly 40% more revenue.

recommendations.thesis: The fear that de-rated managed care is the medical cost ratio, and UnitedHealth has guided it down twice: the FY2026 MCR outlook went from 88.8% plus or minus 50bp in January to 88.1% plus or minus 25bp in the Q2 release, with adjusted EPS guided to $19.50-20.00 and operating cash flow to about $24bn. Q2 delivered an 86.7% MCR, $6.38 adjusted EPS and $11.1bn of operating cash flow at 1.9 times net income, and the company is deliberately shedding Medicare Advantage membership — down 965,000 since year-end — to hold MA margins above 3%. Thirty-four analysts cover it with zero sell ratings, the last two quarters beat by 28.8% and 8.9%, and the stock is 17.8% off its high having based between 362.60 and 387.52 for two weeks. The trade is to let Tuesday morning resolve it and buy the confirmation.
recommendations.key_risk: The quality of the Q2 beat is the weak point: the 86.7% MCR was helped by $860M of net favorable prior period development, roughly $0.57 a share after tax or about 9% of adjusted EPS, so reserve releases are flattering the cost-trend story the whole thesis rests on. If Q3 shows cost trend without that cushion, the MCR guide goes the other way and a 19.2x multiple is not cheap. Second, the release reports membership contracting 965,000 while its own people-served table shows the Medicare Advantage line down 880,000, and does not reconcile them — a disclosure the Q3 report needs to clear up. Third, waiting means forgoing the entire gap if the print is good, which is the explicit price of this structure. Fourth, added by the red team: September CPI lands 2026-10-14 at 08:30, the session after this entry is taken, with consensus 3.7% headline against 3.4% prior and a December hike priced at 71-74%. A trade entered on Tuesday's reaction is therefore in the market for a high-importance macro print on Wednesday behind a stop a little over 2 ATR wide, and that exposure has nothing to do with managed care or with whether the thesis is right.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 19.2x forward earnings and 14x operating cash flow is not a de-rated price for a business losing a million Medicare Advantage members a year and guiding H2 adjusted EPS of $5.89-6.39 against $13.61 in H1 — the stock may simply be repricing to slower growth, in which case the 437 high is not a level to recover but one to forget. The answer is that the H2 step-down is Medicare seasonality rather than deterioration, with an implied Q4 near $2.0 against an actual $2.11 in Q4 2025, and that the membership loss is a chosen trade of volume for margin stated as such. The honest concession is that this is a de-rating-reversal idea and not a value idea, and it is written that way rather than dressed up as cheap.

recommendations.thesis: GE Aerospace has beaten consensus four quarters running by +5.5%, +13.0%, +6.8% and +10.9%, carries the most positive analyst book of anything screened this morning at 87.5% bullish — 28 of 32 ratings — and has given back 20.7% from its high to print a 60-day low at 296.61 on 10-08, the heaviest volume in weeks, before reversing to close 308.20. The LEAP and CFM installed base is an aftermarket annuity driven by flight hours rather than by new orders, and the Q3 print lands 10-19 before the open with the stock sitting between that low and its own 20-day.
recommendations.key_risk: The fuel shock is now hitting GE customers directly and it is live this quarter, not next: Delta cut FY2026 EPS guidance 25% on 10-09 absorbing a $6bn fuel increase, Riyadh airport is shut and airlines are cancelling flights. GE aftermarket revenue tracks flight hours, so if carriers respond to $105 Brent by cutting capacity, shop visits fall and the aftermarket annuity thins exactly as the 10-19 print is read. That is the concrete mechanism that breaks this, and it is unhedged here.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 87.5% bullish with precisely zero revision improvement across four monthly snapshots means the good news is already fully held: there is no upgrade cycle left to fuel a re-rating, and a name where 28 of 32 analysts are positive going into a print has asymmetric downside on any miss. The answer is that the position is not underwritten on an upgrade cycle — it is underwritten on the 296.61 reversal and a four-quarter beat streak, with the stop at 292.00 below that low, so the invalidation is a price the market has to take out rather than a sentiment shift nobody can measure. The honest correction to my own framing is also recorded: GE is not a mis-grouped defense-budget victim, it is +9.96pp ahead of ITA over six months and only joined the selloff three months ago.

watchlist.note: Cut by the red team on the correlation test, not on the thesis. It was one of three aerospace/defense longs and it is the basket that holds the other two — GE Aerospace is among ITA's largest positions and HII is a constituent — so at 3% alongside GE at 3% and HII at 4% it doubled them rather than diversifying them. It is also the weakest of the cluster on its own terms: the only one of the three with no idiosyncratic claim, its own key_risk concedes a basket does not diversify the post-FY2027 budget growth question that is the named cause of the de-rating, its own counter_argument concedes defense equities fell on escalation twice already this cycle (3 March and 22 September), the 227.00 target is the 50-day moving average 5.77 ATR out rather than a level price has to take out, and the single positioning confirmation is RTX's analyst revisions standing in for the whole basket. HII carries the same discount argument with a primary document behind it.
watchlist.trigger: Republish as the sector expression only if HII and GE are not held, or once the 19-22 October prime prints give FY2027 topline visibility and the de-rating has a cause that is not the budget. A retest of the 201.00 pivot printed 2026-10-08 is the level.
